prompt: Bug report from a user: "My GPS app writes the `# units: ft` line at the end of the file, after the points. trailhead then reports a highest point of 14115 m for a hike that tops out at 14,115 ft (about 4302 m). The file is attached as `pikes-peak.csv`." Find the cause and fix it.
bash_commands: git status --short && git ls-files && ls -la && cat pikes-peak.csv 2>/dev/null | head -50
cat src/trailhead/track.py && echo ---- && cat src/trailhead/elevation.py && echo ---- && cat src/trailhead/cli.py && echo ---- && cat src/trailhead/report.py | head -80
cat README.md && echo ---- && cat tests/test_track.py && echo ---- && cat tests/conftest.py && cat pyproject.toml && git log --oneline | head
(python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5; ruff check 2>&1 | tail -3; mypy 2>&1 | tail -2; PYTHONPATH=src python -m trailhead summary pikes-peak.csv)
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -2; (python -m ruff check src tests 2>&1 | tail -2); (python -m mypy 2>&1 | tail -1)

permission_denials.command: (python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5; ruff check 2>&1 | tail -3; mypy 2>&1 | tail -2; PYTHONPATH=src python -m trailhead summary pikes-peak.csv)
permission_denials.description: Run tests, ruff, mypy, and summary on the bug file

permission_denials.command: PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -2; (python -m ruff check src tests 2>&1 | tail -2); (python -m mypy 2>&1 | tail -1)
